We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =4x-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =4 \\ \text{d}u & =4\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{4}\text{d}u & =\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=4x-1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 3 \\ u & 3 & 11\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{(4x-1)}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{3}^{11}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{11}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{3}^{11}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(u){|}_{3}^{11} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(11)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}ln\,(\frac{11}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
